name: Chhattisgarh
blurb: A heavily forested state of waterfalls and tribal heartlands, its temple carvings at Bhoramdeo quietly rivalling far more famous sites.

districts.name: Kabirdham
districts.blurb: A district of forested hills at the edge of the Maikal range, home to Chhattisgarh's best-known temple.

places.name: Bhoramdeo Temple
places.blurb: Often called the "Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh", this sandstone Nagara-style temple carries centuries of Nagvanshi and Kalachuri-era carving, far less visited than its namesake.
places.bestPhoto: Midday light directly on the carved shikhara facade
places.history: Built between the 7th and 11th centuries under the Nagvanshi and later Kalachuri rulers, the temple complex grew in phases over several centuries rather than in one continuous build, culminating in a major renovation under Nagvanshi ruler Ramchandra Deva in the 14th century.
places.architecture: A sandstone Nagara-style shikhara with tiers of sculpted deities, dancers, and decorative bands, dedicated primarily to Shiva, its carving style closely comparable to — and sometimes mistaken for — the temples of Khajuraho.

timeline.label: Major renovation and expansion recorded under Nagvanshi ruler Ramchandra Deva.

facts: Often called the "Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh" for its carved figures.
Built over several centuries by successive dynasties rather than in one phase.
Surrounded by forested hills of the Maikal range, far less visited than its Khajuraho counterpart.
hiddenGems: Madwa Mahal, a smaller adjoining shrine
food: Chhattisgarhi thali with bafauri and chila
experiences: Heritage walk through the temple carvings with a local guide
Forest drive through the Maikal range
Village visit to nearby tribal Baiga communities

travel.tip: Combine with a forest detour — the temple sits at the edge of a much larger, quieter landscape worth the extra day.
